note: Forest Service campground in four wooded loops above the St. Francis River, Missouri's whitewater river, at an old silver mine. Riverside, the only loop with electric, is beside the Highway D bridge with the river 50 to 75 m away through the trees; Prospect and Summit on the hilltop and Spring Branch farther north have no river views. Busiest during spring kayaking; a trail follows both banks. In the old lead-mining district: campsite soils were capped in 2015. --Claude
summary: Read on the FS page and rec.gov: season Mar 5-Nov 1 (closed for the winter now), $15 non-electric / $25 electric, 35 RV sites of 47 (9 electric: eight 30 A, one 50 A double), no water hookups, showers or dump; Spring Branch loop first-come. Stored flat $15 -> $15-25. WATERFRONT LEAD DOWN riverfront -> riverview. policy_ref should be federal:usfs (confirmed FS, concessionaire-managed, on rec.gov).
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD DOWN (stored riverfront, no stored evidence): no site is on an open apron by the river. The Forest Service's own loop list reads 'Riverside: 11 electric hookup sites, views of river, lots of trees'; 'Prospect and Summit adjoined campgrounds: 43 non-electric sites, no river views'; 'Spring Branch: 16 non-electric sites, no river views, wooded'. On the 0.33 m/px leaf-off frame with the catalog coordinates plotted, the Riverside loop is on a wooded flat south-west of the Highway D bridge; its two nearest sites are 011 (about 50 m from the bank) and 009 (about 70 m), with continuous mature trees between the pads and the water and no cleared ground; sites 4-8 are 90-130 m back. The hilltop loops are 250-400 m from the river, Spring Branch 500 m+. Count on an open apron within 50 m: none. Supports RIVERVIEW (the agency states views from the Riverside loop). rec.gov's campsite records carry 'Proximity to Water: Riverfront' on the hilltop and Spring Branch sites as well as the Riverside ones, so that tag is facility-wide and not usable as per-site evidence.

POLICY_REF (apply.py may not write it): the entry has none stored. This is a Mark Twain NF campground sold on recreation.gov -> federal:usfs is right. A concessionaire manages it on site (rec.gov notice: the shelter 'is availalbe through the campground consessionaire... contact the manager at 573-783-3769') but booking and fees are the Forest Service's on recreation.gov, so it is not a policy_ref none case.

PIN: stored 37.5528,-90.4372 is rec.gov's facility point; it falls inside the Riverside (electric) loop, so it is on a camping loop - no move. For the record the loops are spread over 1.4 km: Riverside 37.5527,-90.4367; Prospect/Summit 37.5588,-90.4390 (the FS page's own point is 37.559161,-90.43879); Spring Branch 37.5636,-90.4374. All share the one entrance on Highway D: no split.

FEES CONFLICT (agency page vs rec.gov): the FS page lists 'Single Site with electric hook-up: $20 per night'; recreation.gov's 2026 and 2027 rate tables give STANDARD ELECTRIC $25. rec.gov sells the sites, so $25 is written. Other figures agree ($15 single, $25 double, $35 double electric).

SITE COUNT CONFLICT: the FS page says '70 individual sites: 11 sites with electric hookup, 59 nonelectric sites, 1 group site'; recreation.gov's catalog lists 47 individual sites (9 electric, 26 non-electric RV, 12 tent-only) plus the group site, numbered up to 75 with gaps. Written: 35, the RV sites in the catalog. The FS figure may count decommissioned or doubled sites; unknown.

RESERVABLE CONFLICT: the FS page says 'Nonelectric sites are available first come, first served' and 'Electric Campsites: Reservation needed'; the rec.gov calendar sells the non-electric Prospect/Summit sites too (19 of them 'Available' on 2027-03-10) and marks only Spring Branch and two others 'Not Reservable'. Written from the calendar.

STATUS: closed for the season since Nov 1, 2026 (the FS page shows 'Site Closed'; an ordinary winter closing, no status written). Reopens March 2027. No forest closure order names Silver Mines; the page's standing alert is the lead-soil notice (campsites capped in 2015, risk 'generally considered to be low').
FIT: Spring Branch and the 25-ft Summit/Prospect sites are posted at 25 ft; every RV site is 25 ft or more. FS page: 'Vehicle Clearance: No restrictions', paved spurs. No fit problem.
MIN STAY: 3 nights on holiday weekends only (written); no standing minimum.
